kept.title: Dropped pool_worker case removes the split == pool boundary check
kept.claim: After W8 no positive test covers pool_worker when n_attn_workers equals the pool size (every pool worker runs attention, zero main helpers). The removed case had `CHECK(stats->pool_worker(WORKER_0, N_WORKERS_3) == WORKER_0)` and `CHECK(stats->pool_worker(WORKER_2, N_WORKERS_3) == WORKER_2)`. The remaining rows case uses splits 1 and 2 of a pool of 3; the abort case uses split 4. The equality boundary is what TRON_ASSERT_LE admits and what production reaches when max_main_helpers == 0.
kept.evidence: attn_stats.hpp:431-435 `TRON_ASSERT_LE(n_attn_workers, n_workers); TRON_ASSERT_LT(attn_ix, n_attn_workers); return n_workers - n_attn_workers + attn_ix;`. model.hpp:2006-2007 `if (max_main_helpers == 0) { n_main_helpers = 0;`. Remaining pool_worker calls in tests: t_attn_stats.cpp:431 (split 4 aborts), :433 (attn_ix 2 with split 2 aborts), :660 (split 1), :672 and :675 (split 2). No call with split == N_WORKERS_3 remains.

verdicts.evidence:
Verified against the working tree (committed 0f784c44ff + uncommitted diff).

- The helper admits the equality: attn_stats.hpp:431-435 has `TRON_ASSERT_LE(n_attn_workers, n_workers); TRON_ASSERT_LT(attn_ix, n_attn_workers); return n_workers - n_attn_workers + attn_ix;`.
- The removed test case (diff hunk at t/t_attn_stats.cpp old lines 640-657) carried `CHECK(stats->pool_worker(WORKER_0, N_WORKERS_3) == WORKER_0);` and `CHECK(stats->pool_worker(WORKER_2, N_WORKERS_3) == WORKER_2);`. It also carried an off-state check `off->pool_worker(WORKER_0, SPLIT_1) == WORKER_2` that the diff drops too (not part of this finding).
- Remaining pool_worker calls in t/t_attn_stats.cpp after the diff: :431 (split N_WORKERS_3 + 1, expects SIGABRT), :433 (attn_ix WORKER_2 with split N_WORKERS_3 - 1, expects SIGABRT), :660 (WORKER_0, SPLIT_1), :672 (WORKER_0, SPLIT_2), :675 (WORKER_1, SPLIT_2). The pool is N_WORKERS_3 = 3 (t_attn_stats.cpp:37, :80). No call with split == 3 remains.
- No other test file calls pool_worker directly (grep over t/, h/, src/: only attn_stats.hpp:431 and self_attention.hpp:856/:1344/:1486). t/t_llama_unit.cpp:2192-2230 exercises the row through apply_page_range with a 1-worker split on a pool of `state.self_attn_state.attn.size()`; that equals the split only when the app pool has one worker, which is machine dependent, not a fixed positive check.
- Production reaches the boundary: model.hpp:2006-2007 `if (max_main_helpers == 0) { n_main_helpers = 0;` and model.hpp:1741 documents attention worker i running on pool worker `num_workers() - n_attn_workers + i`, so zero main helpers means n_attn_workers == num_workers. max_main_helpers comes from TRON_MAX_MAIN_HELPERS or num_workers/2 (model.hpp:76-79).

So the claim is true: after W8 the equality boundary of the helper has no positive check in t_attn_stats.cpp. Severity should-fix is fair: the arithmetic is one line, but the case is the one that TRON_ASSERT_LE (not LT) exists for.

Refutation attempt failed on the facts; it partly succeeds on severity. Verified read-only in /home/jhan/workspace/ai-runs/tron-attn-stats (head 0f784c44ff + round5.diff).

Facts that support the finding:
- After the diff, the positive pool_worker calls in t/t_attn_stats.cpp are :660 (WORKER_0, SPLIT_1), :672 (WORKER_0, SPLIT_2) and the new :675 (WORKER_1, SPLIT_2). The abort calls are :431 (split N_WORKERS_3 + 1) and :433 (attn_ix 2 with split 2). No call with split == N_WORKERS_3 remains (grep -n "pool_worker(" over the file).
- The deleted case held `CHECK(stats->pool_worker(WORKER_0, N_WORKERS_3) == WORKER_0)` and `CHECK(stats->pool_worker(WORKER_2, N_WORKERS_3) == WORKER_2)` (round5.diff, removed lines 648-649).
- h/tron/models/attn_stats.hpp:431-435: `TRON_ASSERT_LE(n_attn_workers, n_workers); TRON_ASSERT_LT(attn_ix, n_attn_workers); return n_workers - n_attn_workers + attn_ix;`. The remaining tests cannot distinguish LE from LT on the first assert: splits 1 and 2 of a pool of 3 pass either way, and split 4 aborts either way. Only a split equal to the pool separates them.
- The asserts are always compiled in: h/common/assert.hpp:3-5 undefines NDEBUG. So an LE-to-LT slip would abort in production, not only in test builds.
- Production reaches split == pool: h/tron/models/model.hpp:2006-2007 sets n_main_helpers = 0 when max_main_helpers == 0, and init_max_main_helpers (model.hpp:76-79) returns atol(TRON_MAX_MAIN_HELPERS) or num_workers/2, so TRON_MAX_MAIN_HELPERS=0 or a one-worker pool gives n_attn_workers == num_workers. The production callers self_attention.hpp:856 (after W9), :1343 and :1485 then call pool_worker(i, num_workers).
- t/t_llama_unit.cpp does not pin the boundary deterministically. The :2186-2197 case uses STATS_ON_TRUE with split 1, but the pool size is app_pool().num_workers() (self_attention.hpp:480), so split == pool only on a one-worker host, and the :2254 branch then prints a WARN and skips. The split-queries case (:2612-2713, n_workers = 4, pool = max(attn.size(), 4)) reaches split == pool only when the host pool has <= 4 workers, and its stats object follows TRON_ATTN_STATS (unset in CTest, :2504-2508), so pool_worker is not even called there in the default CTest run.

Scope and maintainer acceptance:
- W8 (verbatim from the scratchpad prompt): the :640 case "adds only the arithmetic of a one-line function, so it could be dropped." The reviewer's objection is to a separate case that re-evaluates the formula, not to the boundary of the assertion. The working tree already grafted one CHECK into the rows case for the same reason (apply.py:119 "keep the '+ attn_ix' term of the formula under a positive check"). Two more lines in the same block, pinning the equality bound of an always-on assertion that production reaches, are the same kind of edit and stay inside W8's scope.
- The wf1.json W8 analysis rated the lost identity-at-full-split checks "not load-bearing" and recommended "No replacement CHECK is needed". That rating looked at the formula value, not at the LE boundary of the assert. The finding's argument is about the assert boundary, which that analysis did not address.

Where the refutation partly succeeds:
- Severity "should-fix" is arguable. The guarded regression (someone tightening LE to LT) is unlikely, and the fix is two CHECK lines. A maintainer would accept it as a nit-level addition; "nice-to-have" would also be a fair label. The claim itself and the fix are correct.
- The proposed placement (inside the forward B braces, after the SPLIT_2 CHECK) mixes a pool-wide statement into the split-2 block. It compiles and reads acceptably, but the boundary checks belong better before forward A, next to the SPLIT_1/SPLIT_2 constants. See corrections.

kept.title: forward_scope test header lost the two-writer failure mode
kept.claim: The old header explained why one owner matters (two writers, the scheduler for forwards + wall and the model for class + job counts + path sets, could file a wall under the wrong class). The new header states what forward_scope does but not what goes wrong without it. The failure mode survives only in the inline comment at :344-345 and in attn_stats.hpp:861-863, so the test body still encodes the why; the header is weaker than before.

verdicts.evidence:
Checked against the working tree of /home/jhan/workspace/ai-runs/tron-attn-stats (git diff = round5.diff) and the committed head 0f784c44ff.

What holds:
- The header at t/t_attn_stats.cpp:306-309 now reads only what forward_scope does (one owner, class at construction, wall + fold at destruction, "So every caller ... gets a whole record filed under the class of that forward"). It contains no negative statement of what a caller without the object gets. The failure is implied by negation only.
- The committed header (git show HEAD:t/t_attn_stats.cpp lines 306-308) named the two writers: "the record behind <class>_forwards had two writers, the scheduler (forwards and the wall) and the model (class, token jobs, path sets)". The working tree drops that clause. grep for "two writers" or "scheduler" in t_attn_stats.cpp now returns nothing.
- The failure mode survives in h/tron/models/attn_stats.hpp:861-863 ("A caller of the hooks without this object gets a half record: token jobs without forwards, or a wall filed under the previous forward's class") and in the test body's inline comment plus the prompt-after-decode block.
- The proposed fix text is present-tense, names no review round, is a hypothetical ("could be filed"), matches the hpp wording, and every line is <= 79 columns (measured 78/75/78/79/77/56). It satisfies W7's scrub rule while restoring the reason.

Why the removal was legitimate but the fix is still an improvement: the dropped clause was past tense ("had two writers") = a description of the pre-fix state, which is exactly what W6/W7 asked to remove. The fix re-states the same reason as a present-tense invariant, so it is compatible with W7.

Nit severity is right: the test body still encodes the why (:343-344 comment + the second scope with prompt_or_mixed after decode_like), so nothing is lost from the test's intent, only from the header.
verdicts.corrections:
Two evidence corrections, no change to the fix text:

The old header (HEAD t/t_attn_stats.cpp:306-308) named the two writers and their fields, but did NOT state the failure mode ("wall under the wrong class") either. That sentence exists only in attn_stats.hpp:862-863, in both HEAD and the working tree. Suggested wording for the claim: "The old header named the two writers (scheduler: forwards + wall; model: class + job counts + path sets). The new header states what forward_scope does and names neither the two-writer split nor what goes wrong without one owner."

2. The inline comment that keeps the failure mode is at t/t_attn_stats.cpp:343-344, not :344-345 (line 343 "// The wall is filed under the class the scope stored, never under the class", line 344 "// of an earlier forward: a prompt forward after a decode forward.").

The fix text as given is acceptable verbatim; every line fits under 80 columns.

verdicts.evidence:

kept.title: Dropped off-state pool_worker check matches the code: no caller computes the key before testing the switch

Checked against the working tree of /home/jhan/workspace/ai-runs/tron-attn-stats (head 0f784c44ff plus the uncommitted diff; git status shows the four modified files).
